title: Yankees’ George Lombard Jr. likely to avoid IL after knee injury scare
content:
NEW YORK — New York Yankees shortstop George Lombard Jr. seems likely to avoid going on the injured list despite twisting his right knee and leaving before the fourth inning of Saturday night’s 9-2 win over the Boston Red Sox.

Lombard said an MRI showed there was no structural damage to his knee, though he felt some soreness on Sunday morning.

“It’s good that it’s nothing too serious,” Lombard said.

The Yankees consider Lombard’s availability to be day to day, though he seemed unlikely to play in Sunday’s series finale, manager Aaron Boone said. José Caballero was in the starting lineup at shortstop.

“They don’t seem too concerned about it,” Boone said. “But we’ve got to get the discomfort out of there and the swelling out of there. We’ll see what we have today.”

“It was just kind of one of those weird freak things,” Lombard said.

Lombard said he felt fine walking around Sunday morning.

“It’s definitely better than (Saturday),” he said. “It felt a little stiff, and there’s still a little soreness and a little inflammation in there. But not terrible.”

It was unclear if Lombard would be ready to play Monday when the Yankees face the Los Angeles Angels on the road.

Lombard suffered the injury while trying to check his swing and avoid getting hit by a 97 mph sinker from Red Sox right-hander Bryan Bello in a 2-2 count with one out and a runner on first base in the second inning.

Lombard singled in the at-bat, played defense in the top of the third inning and batted again in the bottom of that inning. Boone took Lombard out of the game before the start of the fourth, and Lombard went for tests at a nearby hospital, complaining of stiffness.

The 21-year-old had played every inning of every game since he was called up Aug. 4. He’s had ups and downs, hitting .253 with two home runs, six RBIs and a .677 OPS in 23 games. Despite making some highlight-reel defensive plays, he also committed an error in six straight games, a streak that ended Friday.

Lombard is the Yankees’ No. 1 prospect; The Athletic’s Keith Law ranked him as the sixth-best prospect in the game in May.

If Lombard isn’t available Sunday, the Yankees will be without a backup infielder. Third baseman Ryan McMahon (thumb sprain) likely won’t return from the injured list before rosters expand Sept. 1. DH Luis García Jr., regularly a first baseman, played second base for the Washington Nationals in 2025, but is considered a poor defender at the position.

When Lombard debuted, he replaced former Yankees top prospect Anthony Volpe, who hasn’t been called up since. Volpe has mostly played second base at Triple A, but he played third base on Saturday night for the first time.

“The last couple of days,” Boone said, “we started to do some pregame at third just to kind of expand his profile a little bit, expand his versatility a little bit.”
